note: Year 11 Higher Higher Autumn Block 6 Circle theorems: one set of templates per small step of the scheme of learning.

templates.subtopic: Angles in circles
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S1 Angles in circles
templates.text: $O$ is the centre of a circle. Triangle $OAB$ has $OA$ and $OB$ as radii and angle $AOB$ = [[x]]°. Find angle $OAB$.

templates.subtopic: Angles in circles
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S1 Angles in circles
templates.text: A chord $AB$ of a circle centre $O$ has angle $OAB$ = [[y]]°. Find angle $AOB$.

templates.subtopic: Angles in circles
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S1 Angles in circles
templates.text: A circle has radius [[r]] cm. Chord $AB$ subtends angle [[x]]° at the centre $O$. Name the type of triangle $OAB$ and find the other two angles.
templates.answer: Isosceles ($OA = OB$ radii); both base angles [[(180 - x) / 2]]°

templates.subtopic: Angles in circles
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S1 Angles in circles
templates.text: $A$, $B$ and $C$ are on a circle centre $O$. Angle $AOB$ = [[x]]° and angle $BOC$ = [[y]]°. Find angles $OAB$ and $OBC$ and explain why. (3 marks)
templates.answer: $OAB$ = [[(180 - x) / 2]]°; $OBC$ = [[(180 - y) / 2]]° (isosceles triangles with two radii)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles at the centre and circumference)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S2 Circle theorem (angles at the centre and circumference)
templates.text: $A$, $B$ and $C$ are on a circle centre $O$. Angle $ACB$ = [[x]]° at the circumference. Find angle $AOB$ at the centre.
templates.answer: [[2 * x]]° (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles at the centre and circumference)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S2 Circle theorem (angles at the centre and circumference)
templates.text: Angle $AOB$ at the centre of a circle is [[2 * x]]°. Find the angle at the circumference on the same arc $AB$.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles at the centre and circumference)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S2 Circle theorem (angles at the centre and circumference)
templates.text: The angle at the centre standing on an arc is $(4x + [[a]])°$ and the angle at the circumference is $(x + [[b]])°$. Find $x$.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles at the centre and circumference)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S2 Circle theorem (angles at the centre and circumference)
templates.text: $A$, $B$, $C$ are on a circle centre $O$ with angle $ACB$ = [[x]]°. Find angle $OAB$ and justify each step. (4 marks)
templates.answer: Angle $AOB$ = [[2 * x]]° (centre = 2 × circumference); triangle $OAB$ isosceles so angle $OAB$ = [[(180 - 2 * x) / 2]]°

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in a semicircle)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S3 Circle theorem (angles in a semicircle)
templates.text: $[[p]][[q]]$ is a diameter of a circle and $[[c]]$ is on the circumference. What is angle $[[p]][[c]][[q]]$?

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in a semicircle)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S3 Circle theorem (angles in a semicircle)
templates.text: $AB$ is a diameter and $C$ is on the circle. Angle $CAB$ = [[x]]°. Find angle $CBA$.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in a semicircle)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S3 Circle theorem (angles in a semicircle)
templates.text: $AB$ is a diameter. Angle $ABC$ = $(2x + [[a]])°$ and angle $BAC$ = $(x + [[b]])°$. Find $x$.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in a semicircle)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S3 Circle theorem (angles in a semicircle)
templates.text: $AB$ is a diameter of length [[2 * r]] cm and $C$ is on the circle with $AC$ = [[a]] cm. Find $BC$ and the area of triangle $ABC$ to 1 decimal place. (3 marks)
templates.answer: $BC$ = [[sqrt(4 * r * r - a * a)|dp:1]] cm; area [[0.5 * a * sqrt(4 * r * r - a * a)|dp:1]] cm²

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in the same segment)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S4 Circle theorem (angles in the same segment)
templates.text: $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ are on a circle. Angle $ACB$ = [[x]]°. Find angle $ADB$ (same segment).
templates.answer: [[x]]° (angles in the same segment are equal)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in the same segment)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S4 Circle theorem (angles in the same segment)
templates.text: Angles $ACB$ and $ADB$ stand on the same arc $AB$. Angle $ACB$ = $(2x + [[a]])°$ and angle $ADB$ = $(3x - [[b]])°$. Find $x$.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in the same segment)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S4 Circle theorem (angles in the same segment)
templates.text: Two chords $AC$ and $BD$ meet inside a circle. Angle $ACB$ = [[x]]° and angle $CAD$ = [[y]]°. Find angle $ADB$ and angle $CBD$.
templates.answer: Angle $ADB$ = [[x]]° (same segment as $ACB$); angle $CBD$ = [[y]]° (same segment as $CAD$)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in the same segment)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S4 Circle theorem (angles in the same segment)
templates.text: $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ lie on a circle. Angle $ABD$ = [[x]]° and angle $BAC$ = [[y]]°. Use circle theorems to find angle $ACD$ and angle $BCD$ if angle $ABC$ = [[z]]°. (4 marks)
templates.answer: Angle $ACD$ = [[x]]° (angles in the same segment); angle $BDC$ = [[y]]° (same segment as $BAC$)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in a cyclic quadrilateral)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S5 Circle theorem (angles in a cyclic quadrilateral)
templates.text: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle $A$ = [[x]]°. Find angle $C$.
templates.answer: [[180 - x]]° (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in a cyclic quadrilateral)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S5 Circle theorem (angles in a cyclic quadrilateral)
templates.text: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral with angle $B$ = [[x]]° and angle $C$ = [[y]]°. Find angles $D$ and $A$.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in a cyclic quadrilateral)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S5 Circle theorem (angles in a cyclic quadrilateral)
templates.text: $ABCD$ is cyclic. Angle $A$ = $(3x + [[a]])°$ and angle $C$ = $(2x - [[b]])°$. Find $x$ and angle $A$.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angles in a cyclic quadrilateral)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S5 Circle theorem (angles in a cyclic quadrilateral)
templates.text: $ABCD$ is cyclic and $AB$ is extended to $E$. Angle $CBE$ = [[x]]°. Find angle $ADC$ and explain. (3 marks)
templates.answer: Angle $ADC$ = [[x]]° (the exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the opposite interior angle)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angle between radius and tangent)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S6 Circle theorem (angle between radius and tangent)
templates.text: A tangent touches a circle at $[[p]]$ and $O$ is the centre. What is the angle between the tangent and the radius $O[[p]]$?

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angle between radius and tangent)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S6 Circle theorem (angle between radius and tangent)
templates.text: In triangle $OAT$, $AT$ is a tangent at $A$ and $O$ is the centre. Angle $AOT$ = [[x]]°. Find angle $ATO$.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angle between radius and tangent)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S6 Circle theorem (angle between radius and tangent)
templates.text: $AT$ is a tangent to a circle centre $O$ with radius [[r]] cm and $OT$ = [[t]] cm. Find the length $AT$ to 1 decimal place.
templates.answer: $AT$ = [[sqrt(t * t - r * r)|dp:1]] cm (right angle at $A$)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (angle between radius and tangent)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S6 Circle theorem (angle between radius and tangent)
templates.text: A tangent $PT$ touches a circle centre $O$ at $T$. $OT$ = [[3 * k]] cm and $PT$ = [[4 * k]] cm. Find $OP$ and angle $TOP$ to 1 decimal place. (3 marks)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (perpendicular from the centre to a chord)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S7 Circle theorem (perpendicular from the centre to a chord)
templates.text: A perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord $AB$ meets it at $M$. $AB$ = [[2 * a]] cm. Find $AM$.
templates.answer: [[a]] cm (the perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (perpendicular from the centre to a chord)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S7 Circle theorem (perpendicular from the centre to a chord)
templates.text: The radius of a circle is [[r]] cm. A chord is [[2 * a]] cm long. Find the distance from the centre to the chord to 1 decimal place.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (perpendicular from the centre to a chord)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S7 Circle theorem (perpendicular from the centre to a chord)
templates.text: A chord of length [[2 * a]] cm is [[d]] cm from the centre of a circle. Find the radius to 1 decimal place.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (perpendicular from the centre to a chord)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S7 Circle theorem (perpendicular from the centre to a chord)
templates.text: A circle of radius [[5 * k]] cm has a chord [[8 * k]] cm long. Find the distance of the chord from the centre and the area of triangle $OAB$. (3 marks)
templates.answer: Distance [[3 * k]] cm; area [[12 * k * k]] cm²

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (two tangents from a point)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S8 Circle theorem (two tangents from a point)
templates.text: Two tangents $PA$ and $PB$ are drawn from $P$ to a circle. $PA$ = [[a]] cm. Find $PB$.
templates.answer: [[a]] cm (tangents from a point are equal)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (two tangents from a point)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S8 Circle theorem (two tangents from a point)
templates.text: Tangents $PA$ and $PB$ meet at $P$. Angle $APB$ = [[x]]°. Find angle $PAB$.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (two tangents from a point)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S8 Circle theorem (two tangents from a point)
templates.text: Tangents $PA$ and $PB$ touch a circle centre $O$ at $A$ and $B$. Angle $APB$ = [[x]]°. Find angle $AOB$.
templates.answer: [[180 - x]]° (angles $OAP$ and $OBP$ are 90° and angles in a quadrilateral add to 360°)

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (two tangents from a point)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S8 Circle theorem (two tangents from a point)
templates.text: Tangents $PA$ and $PB$ to a circle centre $O$ of radius [[3 * k]] cm. $OP$ = [[5 * k]] cm. Find $PA$ and the area of quadrilateral $OAPB$. (4 marks)
templates.answer: $PA$ = [[4 * k]] cm; area [[2 * 6 * k * k]] cm²

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (alternate segment theorem) (E)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S9 Circle theorem (alternate segment theorem) (E)
templates.text: A tangent at $A$ and a chord $AB$ make an angle of [[x]]°. State the alternate segment theorem and find the angle in the alternate segment.
templates.answer: The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment: [[x]]°

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (alternate segment theorem) (E)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S9 Circle theorem (alternate segment theorem) (E)
templates.text: The angle between a tangent and chord $AB$ is [[x]]°. Find the angle $ACB$ where $C$ is in the alternate segment.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (alternate segment theorem) (E)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S9 Circle theorem (alternate segment theorem) (E)
templates.text: A tangent at $T$ meets chord $TA$ at [[x]]° and chord $TB$ at [[y]]° on the other side. Find angles $TBA$ and $TAB$ in the alternate segments and angle $ATB$.

templates.subtopic: Circle theorem (alternate segment theorem) (E)
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S9 Circle theorem (alternate segment theorem) (E)
templates.text: A tangent $PQ$ touches a circle at $A$. $B$ and $C$ are on the circle. Angle $PAB$ = [[x]]° and angle $QAC$ = [[y]]°. Find angle $BAC$ and angles $ACB$, $ABC$. (4 marks)

templates.subtopic: Solve problems with circle theorems
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S10 Solve problems with circle theorems
templates.text: $A$, $B$, $C$ are on a circle centre $O$ and angle $ABC$ = [[x]]°. Find reflex angle $AOC$.

templates.subtopic: Solve problems with circle theorems
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S10 Solve problems with circle theorems
templates.text: $AB$ is a diameter and $T$ is such that $TA$ is a tangent. Angle $ABC$ = [[x]]° for $C$ on the circle. Find angle $TAC$.

templates.subtopic: Solve problems with circle theorems
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S10 Solve problems with circle theorems
templates.text: A circle theorem proof: explain why angle $[[p]][[c]][[q]]$ = 90° when $[[p]][[q]]$ is a diameter, using the centre $O$ and radii $O[[p]]$, $O[[q]]$, $O[[c]]$.
templates.answer: Triangles $O[[p]][[c]]$ and $O[[q]][[c]]$ are isosceles: angle $O[[p]][[c]]$ = $a$, $O[[q]][[c]]$ = $b$; angles in the triangle: $a + b + (a + b) = 180$, so $a + b = 90°$

templates.subtopic: Solve problems with circle theorems
templates.source: Y11 Higher Autumn B6 Circle theorems · S10 Solve problems with circle theorems
templates.text: $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ are on a circle centre $O$. Angle $AOC$ = [[2 * x]]° and $B$ is on the major arc. Find angle $ABC$ and angle $ADC$ ($D$ on the minor arc). (3 marks)
